The Real Cat Labs · Engineering demonstration

Remember the work.
Remember its limits.

After a restart, an old request can still look relevant. A source-linked ledger checks whether the task is actually authorized to resume.

Deterministic infrastructure demonstration. 24 original synthetic development histories, plus explicitly separate controls. No patient data, model calls or clinical actions. These results test the declared event policy; they do not measure LLM memory quality.
Explore the mechanism

What survived. What still has authority.

Choose a task and memory view. The source timeline shows every target-task event; the retention lane shows exactly which records reached the fresh reader.

1 · Reader proposal
↓
2 · Current ledger authority
↓
3 · Gate outcome

The gate reads the full authoritative ledger. The reader only sees the selected memory. A favorable gate outcome is not credited to the memory renderer.

Read the source text behind this diagram
Where the gate changes a decision

The 72 history/strategy outcomes contain 0 unsafe proposals. Zero unsafe proposals there follows from its authored record lengths, and zero unsafe final actions is a policy invariant. The separate longer-terminal controls produce 3 caught stale resumptions from the actual reader. A real gate-off rerun produces 3 unsafe resumptions. The separate planted stale-request control is explicitly labeled input, not an ablation.

Turn the budget. Watch the packing boundary.

Every point below runs the actual renderer, reader and gate in-process. It is a sensitivity check on the original authored histories, separate from restart evidence.

Observed raw-tail changes

Each bracket connects consecutive measured points. Counts between sampled budgets are not inferred.

  • 220–240 bytes0 → 8 eligible resumptions
  • 243–244 bytes8 → 9 eligible resumptions
  • 284–285 bytes9 → 6 eligible resumptions
  • 287–288 bytes6 → 3 eligible resumptions
  • 380–400 bytes3 → 4 eligible resumptions
  • 400–420 bytes4 → 6 eligible resumptions
  • 460–480 bytes6 → 7 eligible resumptions
  • 480–488 bytes7 → 11 eligible resumptions
  • 488–489 bytes11 → 12 eligible resumptions
  • 541–542 bytes12 → 9 eligible resumptions
  • 734–735 bytes9 → 10 eligible resumptions
  • 740–741 bytes10 → 11 eligible resumptions
  • 745–746 bytes11 → 12 eligible resumptions

The points use authored histories and whole-record packing; these are not model scores. More budget can retain distracting notes before the current instruction fits. The original matrix has no unsafe proposals by construction. In the longer-terminal family, timeline can also propose stale resumptions at smaller budgets: it needs the gate too.

Download the figure with its scope · Download every measured point and case decision

A visible boundary between memory and permission

Immutable-by-API snapshotFresh-process restoreBudgeted memoryFresh-process proposalEvidence gate

The reader receives only selected records. The gate separately verifies the latest authoritative event. A remembered instruction cannot grant itself permission.

Every outcome, with its denominator

Raw tail retrieves the newest records for the target task. Timeline retrieves its newest authoritative events. Both use a 640-byte context ceiling. Full history is an unbudgeted diagnostic. Resume columns use eligible tasks as their denominator; abstentions use all histories. In the original matrix there are no unsafe proposals, so every resume is eligible.

MemoryHistoriesResume proposalsIneligible resumed before gateResumptions after gateIneligible resumed after gateAbstentions

full_history2412/120/1212/120/120/24

Try to break the boundary

These direct gate probes identify their inputs and exact reasons. The planted row is input, not an ablation. The longer-terminal controls above rerun actual restore and propose workers with the gate enabled and bypassed; their records are in results.json.

ControlObserved outcomeEvidence
Stale request after completionholdstale_evidence
Proposal before gate (planted)resumeThis is the authored input, not an ablation result. The actual gate-off rerun is recorded separately.
